name: EP-10 Platform Super Admin (Backlog)
w: Operator tooling for the SaaS owner: see every hostel and owner account, support a customer without asking for their password, suspend or restore a hostel, manage its plan, and see how the platform is doing. Admin power is dangerous in a multi-tenant system, so every admin action is authenticated with MFA, explained with a reason and written to an immutable audit log the customer can see. Still backlog: schedule it before the first paying hostel, because support and suspension are needed from day one of selling.
ac: E10-T1 Bootstrap platform admins with MFA, never through the app
E10-T2 Admin area and server-side access guard
E10-T3 Immutable admin audit log
E10-T4 Customer directory: owners, hostels and usage
E10-T5 Read-only support view into a hostel, with a reason, shown to the owner
E10-T6 Suspend and restore a hostel, with defined behaviour
E10-T7 Plan and subscription state per account (with EP-14)
E10-T8 Platform metrics dashboard
E10-T9 Account support actions without seeing passwords
E10-T10 Data export and erasure requests (DPDP Act 2023)
E10-T11 Platform announcements to owners
E10-T12 Security tests that tenants can never reach admin functions
out: No impersonation that can write data on behalf of a customer. Billing hostels and payment collection are EP-14; this epic only shows and changes plan state.
dod: Not started. Every task below has its own acceptance criteria; the epic closes when all are done and the admin RLS tests pass in CI.

name: Bootstrap platform admins with MFA, never through the app
w: A platform admin can read every hostel's residents and money. The role must never be grantable from inside the product, and a stolen admin password alone must not be enough.
ac: profiles.role = 'platform_admin' can only be set by a SQL migration or an operator script run with the service role; no app screen or API path can grant it
Admin sign-in requires TOTP MFA through Supabase Auth; admin pages and functions require a session at aal2
Removing the role takes effect on the admin's next request, not at token expiry
docs/admin.md explains how to add and remove an admin, and who is allowed to

name: Build the admin area and its server-side access guard
w: The admin area is a separate surface with its own layout, so tenant screens never gain admin behaviour by accident and admin queries never run for a tenant.
ac: Admin pages live under their own route group (/admin) with their own layout and navigation
Middleware and a server-side requirePlatformAdmin() guard both protect it; non-admins get a 404, not a 403, so the area is not advertised
Admin data access goes through SECURITY DEFINER functions that check private.is_platform_admin() first, never through the service role key in request handlers
Admin pages are excluded from the tenant hostel switcher and active-hostel cookie

name: Record every admin action in an immutable audit log
w: Customers will only trust support access if every look and every change is on record. The log is also how the operator answers 'who did this?' months later.
ac: admin_audit_log records actor, action, target hostel or account, reason, request id and time for every admin read of customer data and every admin change
Rows are written by the admin functions themselves (not by the client) and cannot be updated or deleted, following the allocation_events pattern
A reason is required for viewing a hostel, suspending, restoring, changing a plan and every support action
The log is searchable in the admin area by hostel, admin and date

name: Customer directory: owners, hostels and usage
w: The first question after selling is 'who are my customers and are they using it?'. This answers it without opening the database.
ac: Lists every owner account with email, sign-up date, email confirmed, last sign-in and number of hostels
Lists every hostel with owner, status (draft, active, suspended), city, beds, active residents, invoices this month and last activity date
Search by owner email, hostel name, city or phone; filter by status and plan; paginated in the database
Draft hostels that never finished onboarding are visible, to follow up on stalled sign-ups

name: Read-only support view into a hostel, shown to its owner
w: Support usually means seeing exactly what the customer sees. It must never become a way to change their data, and the owner should be able to see that support looked.
ac: An admin can open a hostel's rooms, residents, occupancy and fees read-only, after entering a reason
No write action, form or server action is reachable from the support view; database functions refuse writes from an admin session to customer tables
Each support session is logged (E10-T3) and the owner sees 'Hostel ERP support viewed your hostel on <date>: <reason>' in their settings
Resident ID numbers stay masked to last 4 and ID proof files cannot be opened from the support view

name: Suspend and restore a hostel, with defined behaviour
w: Suspension already exists as a status and the app now explains it, but nothing sets it and its meaning is not defined. Owners need to know exactly what happens and that no data is lost.
ac: Admins suspend or restore a hostel with a reason; the change is audited
Suspended means: the hostel disappears from the app for owner and staff (the current behaviour), no data is deleted, and invoices or payments cannot be written for it
The owner gets an email naming the hostel and how to contact support; restoring sends a confirmation
Decide and document whether owners keep read-only access or data export while suspended (needed for EP-14 non-payment)

name: Show and change plan and subscription state per account
w: Plans and billing live in EP-14; the admin needs to see them in the customer directory and make manual corrections, such as an extended trial or a complimentary plan.
ac: The customer directory shows each account's plan, subscription status, trial end and next billing date
Admins can extend a trial, apply a complimentary plan or correct a plan, with a reason; changes are audited
Manual changes never bypass the payment gateway's records; they are recorded as admin adjustments

name: Platform metrics dashboard
w: Aggregate numbers tell the operator whether the business is working: sign-ups, activation, usage and, once EP-14 lands, revenue.
ac: Sign-ups per week, onboarding completion rate, hostels active in the last 30 days
Total beds, occupied beds and residents managed across the platform
Invoices generated and payments recorded per month across all hostels (counts and totals)
MRR, active subscriptions, trial conversion and churn once EP-14 exists
Computed by admin-only database functions; no customer names on the dashboard

name: Account support actions without seeing passwords
w: The most common support requests are 'I never got the email' and 'I can't sign in'. The operator should resolve them without ever knowing or setting a password.
ac: Resend the sign-up confirmation email for an unconfirmed owner
Send a password reset email; admins can never set or read a password
Change an owner's email address only through Supabase's confirm-both-addresses flow
Sign an owner out of every device (for a lost phone)
Each action requires a reason and is audited

name: Handle data export and erasure requests under the DPDP Act 2023
w: Hostels store residents' personal data and KYC references. Under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 the platform must be able to export and erase that data on a valid request, and keep only what the law requires. Expensive to retrofit, so it is designed here.
ac: An owner can export all of a hostel's data (rooms, residents, stays, invoices, payments) as CSV or JSON in one archive
Erasure of a resident removes or irreversibly anonymises personal fields and their ID proof file, while keeping the financial records the law requires (amounts, dates, invoice numbers)
Closing an owner account schedules deletion of their hostels after a documented retention period, with a final export offered first
Requests and their completion are logged; docs/data-protection.md records retention periods. Confirm the retention rules with a lawyer before release
out: No consent-management UI for residents in this task.

name: Platform announcements to owners
w: Planned maintenance, new features and policy changes need to reach every owner inside the app.
ac: Admins create an announcement with a message, severity and start and end time
Owners and staff see it as a dismissible banner in the app shell; dismissal is remembered per user
Announcements are audited

name: Prove that tenants can never reach admin functions
w: Admin functions bypass tenant isolation by design. A test suite has to prove the boundary holds for owners, staff and signed-out users, every time CI runs.
ac: RLS and integration tests call every admin function and admin route as an owner, a staff member and anonymously, and expect refusal
An admin without MFA (aal1) is refused too
Tests check that the support view cannot write customer data
The suite runs in CI with the other RLS tests
